name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
role: President of the Syrian Arab Republic for the transitional period (رئيس الجمهورية العربية السورية); head of state and of the executive, as the March 2025 Constitutional Declaration abolished the post of prime minister
party: No party; led Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (هيئة تحرير الشام, HTS) until its dissolution was announced in January 2025
bio: Ahmed Hussein al-Sharaa (أحمد حسين الشرع), born in Riyadh in 1982 to a Syrian family from the Golan Heights and raised in Damascus, has been President of Syria for the transitional period since 29 January 2025, when the commanders of the armed factions that overthrew Bashar al-Assad named him at the 'Victory of the Syrian Revolution' conference; under the Constitutional Declaration he signed on 13 March 2025 there is no prime minister, and the president leads the executive during a five-year transition. Known until December 2024 by his nom de guerre Abu Mohammad al-Jolani (also spelled al-Julani or al-Golani), he joined al-Qaeda in Iraq after the 2003 US-led invasion, was held by US forces in Iraq from about 2005–2006 until 2011, founded the Nusra Front (Jabhat al-Nusra) as al-Qaeda's Syrian branch in 2012, announced a break with al-Qaeda in 2016 and from 2017 led Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), which ran Idlib through the Syrian Salvation Government and led the November–December 2024 offensive that toppled Assad. He was listed by the UN Security Council's ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions committee and designated a terrorist by the United States, which also offered a $10 million reward for him; the reward was withdrawn in December 2024 and the UN and US sanctions on him were lifted in November 2025, days before he became the first Syrian president received at the White House. As of October 2026 his presidency has seen the lifting of most Western sanctions, the repeal of the US Caesar Act and Syria's removal from the US list of state sponsors of terrorism (August 2026), the return of about 1.8 million refugees according to UNHCR, and the integration and dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces in 2026 after a government offensive. It has also seen mass killings of Alawite civilians on the coast in March 2025 and of Druze and Bedouin civilians in Sweida in July 2025, in which the UN Commission of Inquiry found violations by government forces and affiliated fighters, as well as by other armed groups, that may amount to war crimes; continued Israeli military operations in southern Syria; and the indirect selection of a People's Assembly, a third of it appointed by him, which first met in July 2026. No national election had been scheduled as of October 2026; he has said elections could take about four years from the fall of Assad.
